item.title: Pharmaceutical industry drove growth in Danish economy in 2025
item.description: The Danish economy grew by 2.9 percent in 2025, according to Statistics Denmark, and the pharmaceutical industry played a significant role in the growth. Measured by gross value added, the total Danish economy grew by 3.2 percent last year. Without the contribution from the pharmaceutical industry, the increase would have been 1.7 percent. A rise […]

item.title: Tens of thousands of people spend more than a year searching for a job before finding one
item.description: For very young people, finding a job usually takes less time, but a quick placement does not always match their long-term career goals. At the same time, hundreds of thousands of working-age people in Denmark are unemployed and not actively seeking work.

item.title: Commuter lines to run fewer trains next week in several parts of Denmark
item.description: DSB says several train lines in Denmark will have fewer or no direct trains next week because of maintenance needs caused by cold weather. The changes affect lines in East Jutland, South Zealand, and between Copenhagen Airport and Slagelse and Odense. The line between Nykøbing Falster and Copenhagen Airport will also be affected. The changes […]

item.title: Government launches 1.2 billion DKK national preparedness strategy, calls on residents to prepare for crises
item.description: The package funds healthcare, water security, telecommunications, municipalities and Greenland. Ministers say stronger coordination is needed, and households should be prepared to manage independently during crises.

item.title: New record for travelers crossing the Øresund
item.description: In 2025, passenger trips across the Øresund by car, train, and ferry exceeded 40 million for the first time, averaging 112,309 daily journeys – a 6.7 percent increase. item.title: Commuter routes will see fewer train departures next week
item.description: From February 23 to March 1, DSB will reduce train services across East Jutland, South Zealand, and routes connecting Copenhagen Airport to Odense. The company cites a shortage of operational trains caused primarily by recent cold winter weather and increased maintenance needs. item.title: Four sperm whales stranded near Fanø
item.description: Sperm whales are the world’s largest toothed whales. Strandings of sperm whales along Danish coasts are unusual. Environment Minister Magnus Heunicke said it is very important that the public respects any cordons around the site. “Disturbances can stress the animals and make a possible rescue more difficult,” he said.

item.title: Archaeology in Denmark: Ten discoveries unearthed in 2025
item.description: Every year, construction projects, plowed fields and scientific studies uncover traces of Denmark’s long history. In 2025, archaeologists across the country made a series of discoveries that shed new light on life from the Neolithic Age to the Middle Ages. item.title: Greenlandic websites attacked by Russian hacker group during King Frederik’s visit
item.description: Greenlandic websites are currently experiencing DDoS attacks aimed at overloading networks and making them inaccessible. The Agency for Social Security is monitoring the situation alongside Danish and Greenlandic authorities. The Russian hacker group NoName057(16) claimed responsibility, stating the attacks are retaliation for Denmark’s donation of fighter jets to Ukraine. The group, active since March 2022, […]

item.title: Cycling in Denmark, explained
item.description: You won’t catch me on a bike in the endless winter months, but apparently 80% of Danes still bike, rain or shine, frost or snow. This does not surprise me, when you think that nothing stopped the Vikings from getting into open boats and crossing the Atlantic in all weathers, writes Vivienne McKee.
